title: Protocol for electrotaxis of large epithelial cell sheets
protocol: Precoat the area between each strip with 0.5 mL FNC at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Remove the FNC coating mix with a pipette.
Wash the area with PBS one time.
Air-dry the coating area.
Gently attach sterilized PDMS stencils between the strips in the cell culture dish.
Add silicone grease around the PDMS stencils to create two reservoirs for storing cell suspension.
Avoid air bubbles between the PDMS and the cell culture dish for a firm attachment.
Prepare a cell suspension at a concentration of 8×106 cells/mL.
Add 1 mL of cell suspension for each cell patterning reservoir.
Gently move the dish to an incubator and allow cells to attach for 15 min.
Observe the cells with a microscope to ensure the desired cell density.
Gently remove the medium containing any unattached cells with a pipette.
Add fresh cell culture medium and incubate cells overnight (∼16 h).
Observe the pattern of cell sheets with a microscope.
Confirm whether a confluent monolayer is formed.
Using a pipette, remove the cell culture medium from the reservoirs.
Gently peel off the stencil with tweezers.
Gently wash the patterned cell sheet with the culture medium.
Using a microscope, examine the pattern of the cell sheets.
Confirm that they are in the desired size and shape.
Add 0.5 mL cell culture medium in the area between PDMS strips.
Gently place cover glasses over the stimulation area of the chamber.
Seal the stimulation chamber into two reservoirs by placing silicone grease on top of the cover glasses.
Add 6 mL fresh cell culture medium in each reservoir.
Melt the 1.5% agar in 1× Steinberg solution by microwave.
Slowly fill the melted agar in the glass bridge.
Leave the salt bridge at room temperature to solidify.
Preheat the incubator of the living cell imaging system (37°C, 5% CO2).
Move the electrotaxis chamber into the incubator of the living cell imaging system.
Fill two beakers with 1× Steinberg’s solution.
Connect the electrotaxis system including power supply, electrodes, salt bridges, beakers with saline, electrotaxis chamber, and wires.
Switch on the DC power supply.
Monitor the voltage using a multimeter inserted at both ends of the coverslip in the EF stimulation chamber.
Adjust the total voltage of the current supply to achieve 10.0 V between the two ends of the cover glass.
Switch off the DC power supply.
Cover the cell culture dish with a sterilized lid containing holes.
Align the electrotaxis chamber with the motorized loading stage of the microscope.
Ensure that the applied electric field is parallel to one edge of the stage.
Note the relative position of the cathode and anode in the electrotaxis system.
Start the image acquisition software and set up parameters for time-lapse imaging.
Select a 10× phase contrast objective lens for imaging.
Bring the imaging window of the stimulation chamber into focus.
Navigate to a corner of the well-patterned cell sheet and save the position in the image acquisition system.
Navigate a series of XY positions to cover the whole cell sheet with 20% overlap along x and y axes.
Navigate to other cell sheets in the chamber and save their positions in the imaging acquisition system.
Click the acquisition button to start image recording.
Stop image recording after finishing the first frame of all ROIs.
Check the quality of the images to confirm that the focus and exposure are set correctly.
Monitor for any shift during multi-position acquisition.
Set the time interval to 5 min and duration to 7 h.
Ensure 9 ROI with 20% overlap are used for a square cell sheet up to 1 mm × 1 mm in size.
Control the time spent on setting up the electrotaxis system within about 1 hour.
Perform real-time imaging with precisely controlled EF stimulation.
Click the acquisition button again to start multi-position time-lapse recording.
Switch on the DC power supply at the desired time.
Monitor and adjust voltage during stimulation as needed.
Check that all stage positions remain in focus throughout later points of the experiment.
Stop image acquisition at a defined time point.
Switch off the computer and microscope system.
Apply EF 1 hour after the end of time-lapse recording.
Pause imaging recording if refocusing is needed during long recordings.
Adjust focus and resume imaging within a few seconds to up to a couple of minutes without stopping EF stimulation.
Generate time-lapse movies using ImageJ software.
Launch ImageJ program and import imaging file through ‘File>Import>Image sequence’.
Adjust brightness and/or contrast by clicking ‘Image>Adjust>Brightness/Contrast’.
Stitch images together using Grid/Collection Stitching plugin in ImageJ.
Correct slight shifts in the images using Registration-Register Virtual Stack plugin in ImageJ.
Save video as single ‘.tiff’ files.
